subject: infra.store
name: Data-centre facilities in Morocco
milestone: Reconciled 2026-08-10: the '23' count's rule identified as Uptime Tier-certification, 2023-09-15; no current national facility count established
position_start: 23 Uptime Institute Tier-certified data centres nationally - 11 Casablanca-Settat, 8 Rabat-Sale-Kenitra, 4 Marrakech-Safi (Conseil de la concurrence monograph, Uptime Institute data as at 2023-09-15)
position_end: No national facility count on file with an established counting rule. The widely-repeated '23, ahead of South Africa' figure is that 2023 Tier-certification count, not a current facility census, and the 'ahead of South Africa' claim is a certification-count comparison, not a capacity or estate-size one - the base's capacity evidence (South Africa 60%-plus of Africa's 500-plus MW) does not support continental leadership on size. Other published counts use unstated rules and are not commensurable with the certification figure or each other: 8 active, Casablanca only (Heirs Technologies 'Africa's Digital Leap', 2025); 25-plus, Casablanca only (US Commercial Service, 2025-07-31); 14 nationally at 1.5 MW (BMI/Fitch Solutions, 2026 Q2, not held - capacity figure fails a sanity check against CESE's 98 MW 2020 series and is not ingested).
note: Resolved reviews/contradictions/open/morocco-data-centre-count.md 2026-08-10: 23 and 8 measure different things at different dates, not one contested fact. No ANRT, ADD or Ministry of Digital Transition facility register found. Heirs Technologies report now held in full 2026-08-10 (acquisition pass): staged as [[2026-08-10 Heirs Technologies Africas Digital Leap Cloud Connectivity AI report]]. Its own text states no explicit counting rule for the 8 figure beyond attributing country counts to third-party aggregator Data Center Map and describing facilities by operator ("Morocco supports 8 centers, primarily in Casablanca, led by telcos and regional cloud integrators") - it does not define active/certified/colocation, so the 8 and the Conseil de la concurrence's 23-certified count remain not shown to be reconcilable populations from this source.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Disclosure of security and intelligence personnel records
milestone: Security directorates denied intrusion, 2026-08-27
position_end: A hacking group published on Telegram on 24 August 2026 what it presented as the names, identification numbers and dates of birth of 70,000 police and intelligence personnel. The national security and territorial surveillance directorates categorically denied on 27 August any intrusion into their information systems or security databases, which they said meet the strictest cybersecurity standards, and stated that the published personal data was old material downloaded from databases and information systems run by insurance companies and social and health cover bodies; the same statement warned against circulating doctored photographs presented as security personnel and falsified documents presented as security documents. No third party has verified either the data or the attribution, and no named insurer or cover body has answered
note: what is established is the publication and the denial, not the provenance: the directorates place the source outside their own systems, in insurance and social-cover databases, and no regulator, insurer or cover body has confirmed or denied that. The data-protection commission has published nothing on it

subject: geopol.india
name: Indian cooperation on national-language artificial intelligence
milestone: Joint commission agreed in Rabat, 2026-08-24
position_end: The two governments' digital ministers met in Rabat on 24 August 2026 and agreed to establish a joint commission, its initial focus language technologies and their use in interactions between citizens and government administrations, exploring solutions carrying multiple languages, variants and dialects so public services reach different linguistic communities. They also discussed collaboration around the JAZARI artificial-intelligence institutes; the meeting builds on one in New Delhi in February 2026 on the margins of the AI Impact Summit. No instrument, membership, budget, work programme or timetable for the commission is published
note: an agreement to establish a commission rather than a signed instrument; the account is a trade report of a ministerial meeting, and nothing establishes when or whether the commission convenes
